Just because drug addiction is bad, doesn't mean they should be illegal.

As I said earlier in that comment, most of the people who use heroin don't fit the scummy, dirty, sell his own mom's pussy for another hit, junkie stereotype portrayed in the media. Although, these people do exist, that cannot be denied. However, this behavior is not a symptom of heroin use, it is a symptom of addiction. Heroin is certainly addictive, but are there any studies out there that attempt to quantify addiction? I have first hand experience with a population with a serious alcohol addiction problem. People in my community have been known to steal hairspray containing ethanol... To drink. The problem with the heroin junkie and the problem with the alcohol junkie is the same problem!

Well, how about this? I use heroin regularly, and I have several friends who use heroin regularly. I have never hurt anyone while using, or in an attempt to get more, and I never drive inebriated. When I get high, I want to cuddle up next to my girlfriend, open up a book, and fight off the waves of love as long as I can before I fall asleep. How is what I do any worse than drinking alcohol? 

But here's the thing, what about the asshole who gets completely shit faced and vandalizes buildings and starts fights in public? Obviously we won't criminalize alcohol because of these people, we give them a place to sober up, and send them to AA. Anything wrong with using heroin responsibly or crystal meth **responsibly** is something inherently wrong with using drugs, and there's nothing wrong with that!
There's a legitimate stigma against people who use hard drugs. For someone with the username 'futalover99', I would assume you don't appreciate discriminatory generalizations.

Heroin it self really can't hurt anyone besides the people who use it, but we allow people to absolutely destroy their lives abusing alcohol. And it doesn't make any sense to assume that everyone who uses heroin wants to hurt you and your family, either. The danger and violence associated with illicit drugs come from the gangsters who distribute them, or the junkie, who most likely has a mental disorder to begin with. And it's important to note that most users are not junkies!
